summary: Iteration 80 — Double-charge fix (webhook-independent reconcile + duplicate-payment guard + ACH processing state) verified end-to-end. BACKEND: 6/6 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration80_duplicate_guard.py against the live preview API. (a) POST /api/payments/checkout as demo@jaleter.com (active premium) → 200 {already_active:true} with NO url field (no second Checkout Session created). (b) POST /api/payments/checkout as a freshly-registered user with membership_processing:true and no stripe_customer_id → 200 {processing:true} with NO url (duplicate-payment guard short-circuits). (c) GET /api/user/membership as demo → {active:true, processing:false, status:'active'}. (d) GET /api/user/membership as the flagged user (WITHOUT ?refresh=1 so the flag survives) → {active:false, processing:true, status:'inactive'}. (e) Regression: GET /api/accounts → 402 for the flagged unpaid user (detail.error='payment_required'), 200 for demo (accounts list). FRONTEND (390×844 mobile viewport, Expo web preview): (1) PROCESSING UI: registered a fresh throwaway user, set {membership_processing:true} directly in Mongo, logged in via UI → paywall renders with paywall-processing amber card ('Payment Processing. Your payment is on its way. Bank payments can take a few business days to clear — Jaleter will unlock automatically once Stripe confirms it. Please don't pay again.'), paywall-checkout button is DISABLED (aria-disabled='true') with label 'Payment processing — no need to pay again', and tapping paywall-refresh shows the friendly processing notice ('No need to pay again — bank payments can take a few business days to clear. Jaleter unlocks automatically the moment Stripe confirms it.') — NOT the 'couldn't find an active membership' wording. Button remains disabled after refresh. (2) NORMAL UNPAID: after clearing the flag on the same user, paywall-processing is absent, paywall-checkout enabled with label 'Continue to Jaleter.com', tapping paywall-refresh shows the standard notice 'We couldn't find an active membership on this account yet…'. (3) ACTIVE MEMBER: demo@jaleter.com login lands directly on dashboard (home-profile visible, 'Good evening, Jaleter.' greeting, Jaleter Coach card, Right Now stats, Legacy card) — paywall never shown. All three review-request UI flows confirmed. Zero PAGEERRORs; only expected 402s on gated /api/accounts + /api/notifications/... for the unpaid users (paywall contract) and the standard expo-notifications/shadow-deprecated warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1817-1835 duplicate-payment guard has the correct short-circuit order: (1) re-read user from DB (avoid stale JWT snapshot), (2) has_active_membership() → already_active, (3) reconcile_membership_from_stripe() then re-check active → self-heals missed webhooks, (4) rec.processing OR persisted membership_processing → {processing:true}. Only reaches Checkout Session create when the user is neither active nor processing. Correct.

server.py:1976-2013 user_membership: refresh=0 is a pure read (won't clear a synthetic flag), refresh=1 calls reconcile_membership_from_stripe first. `processing` is exposed as `bool(fresh.get('membership_processing')) and not active` — mutually exclusive with active. Correct contract.

stripe_service.py:414 ACH: checkout.session.completed sets membership_processing = (payment_status not in ('paid','no_payment_required')) — matches the review-request semantics. stripe_service.py:431-445 async_payment_succeeded/failed both clear the flag, plus success re-applies the subscription. stripe_service.py:452-457 invoice.paid also clears the flag as a belt-and-braces. Idempotent.

stripe_service.py:494-525 reconcile_membership_from_stripe correctly returns early when user has no stripe_customer_id (so a user with a synthetic processing flag but no Stripe customer is left untouched by refresh — matches the fixture-safety notes in the review). Best-sub ranking prefers active>trialing>past_due>incomplete>paused and breaks ties by current_period_end. `processing = best.status == 'incomplete'` correctly persists on refresh.

PaywallScreen.tsx:140-165 paywall-processing card renders only when processing state is true, paywall-checkout is disabled iff (busy || processing) and its label reflects the processing state — exactly per spec. paywall-refresh handler (line 79) shows PROCESSING_MSG when processing is set (not the 'couldn't find' copy). Correct.

usePayment.ts:38-39 short-circuits on both {already_active} and {processing} responses BEFORE reading `url`, so a well-behaved server response cannot open a second Checkout tab even if the button were somehow tapped. Belt-and-braces.

Note (informational): current_period_start/end are read at sub.get('current_period_start') on the top-level Subscription object (stripe_service.py:304-317). Stripe API v2024-06-20+ moved these under items.data[0].period, and Stripe's reconcile code at :511 already handles it correctly (`items[0].get('current_period_end')`). _apply_subscription still uses the top-level field — for the accounts I tested (demo, incomplete new-user path) both paths produced correct behavior, but if a future API upgrade drops the top-level fields the period_end column in the DB could become null. Not a blocker for the current fix scope.

app/index.tsx: on paywall mount + AppState 'active', checkMembership(reconcile:true) refreshes from Stripe → this correctly self-heals a user who paid in a separate tab, but for a user with membership_processing=true AND a stripe_customer_id, if Stripe has no incomplete sub, reconcile will clear the flag (which is the intended behavior per the review note). Non-issue — matches spec.

success_rate.backend: 100% (6/6 pytest: already_active + processing + membership status + accounts paywall regression)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 3 review-request UI flows: processing paywall + normal unpaid + active member dashboard)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration80_duplicate_guard.py -v (6 tests, ~2.3s). GOTCHA: the backend LOWERCASES emails at /api/auth/register, so any Mongo update by email in a test fixture must use the lowercased email or matched_count will be 0. The preview backend and this container share the same Mongo (verified: alex+test1@jaleter.app row exists in local Mongo under MONGO_URL). To reproduce the processing UI: register a fresh user (lowercase email), then in Mongo `db.users.update_one({email:<lower>}, {'$set': {membership_processing: True}, '$unset': {stripe_customer_id: '', stripe_subscription_id: '', subscription_status: ''}})` — the $unset of stripe_customer_id is REQUIRED, otherwise the paywall mount auto-reconcile hits Stripe (no incomplete sub for that customer) and clears the flag. Do NOT test with alex+test1 for processing UI — he has stripe_customer_id cus_VC79sS7yOdzPJ9. STRIPE IS LIVE — never complete a real checkout; only inspect the checkout endpoint's JSON. When calling /api/user/membership to verify the processing flag, do NOT pass ?refresh=1 (that would reconcile and clear a synthetic flag). Welcome screen is in an about:srcdoc iframe — iterate page.frames() and click #btnLogin.
rca_of_issue: N/A — main-agent fixes are correct at every layer. Root cause of the original $90 double-charge bug (user reported): the webhook that would have flipped subscription_status→active was missed (or the ACH payment was still clearing), so /api/user/membership kept returning active:false, the UI kept showing the paywall with a Continue button, and the user tapped it a second time → second Checkout Session → second successful charge. All three layers of the fix now defend against this: (a) reconcile_membership_from_stripe queries Stripe directly on paywall-mount + app-foreground + Refresh Membership + inside the /payments/checkout entry, so a missed webhook self-heals; (b) POST /api/payments/checkout returns already_active/processing WITHOUT creating a new Session, so even a rapid double-tap or a mis-cached UI state cannot produce a second charge; (c) ACH-in-flight payments set membership_processing on the user via checkout.session.completed(unpaid), the paywall renders the disabled 'Payment processing' state so the user is never invited to re-tap, and the flag is cleared by async_payment_succeeded / async_payment_failed / invoice.paid.
